entities.name: Ibn Abi al-Khisal
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abū ʿAbdallāh Muḥāmmad ibn Masʿūd ibn Ṭayyīb ibn Faraj ibn Khālaṣa al-Ghāfiqī ash-Sheqūrī, known as Ibn 'Abī'l-Khisāl, was a prominent Andalusī secretary, historian, muhaddith and poet of the medieval Islamic world.

Born in Al-Andalus (present-day Spain) in the 12th century, Ibn 'Abī'l-Khisāl rose to prominence as a senior minister in the court of Caliph Al-Mustadiʿ, earning him the honorific title of Dhū al-Wizāratayn.

As a historian, Ibn 'Abī'l-Khisāl compiled the 'Kitāb Dhakhaīr al-ʿArab', a comprehensive history of the Arabs from the 5th to the 12th centuries, which became a foundational text for later historians.

Ibn 'Abī'l-Khisāl's legacy extends beyond his historical works, as his poetry and prose influenced the literary traditions of the Islamic world.

The poet's works also reveal his deep understanding of the Andalusian context, reflecting the complex cultural and intellectual exchanges between the Islamic world and Europe during the medieval period.

In the years following his death in 1146, Ibn 'Abī'l-Khisāl's works continued to be studied and translated by scholars across the Islamic world, ensuring his significance as a major figure in the intellectual and cultural landscape of medieval Andalusia.

Ibn 'Abī'l-Khisāl's life and work serve as a testament to the enduring power of Islamic learning and culture in shaping the course of human history.
